title: Four widgets are exported from the app barrel but have zero call sites — dead UI shipping in the binary
summary:
Three of the four were already deleted by a later wave (object_info_panel.dart, tour_selection_sheet.dart, sequence_controls.dart are gone, with no barrel exports left) and VariablePickerButton had been wired into the live-stacking watermark field. But that wiring introduced a NEW defect and left the finding's real capability gap open, so this entry is a fix, not already-correct.

1. WRONG VOCABULARY (regression introduced by the earlier fix). The watermark picker was handed `interpolationCatalog` — the SEQUENCER's expression catalog. The watermark speaks a different, much smaller language: a flat token map in LiveStackingBroadcastService._watermarkTokens (target, target.name, integration.hms, integration.secs, frames, stack, stack.method, now), and expandWatermarkTokens (share_card_renderer.dart:714-733) renders an unresolved token LITERALLY. None of the four tokens the field's own helper text names even exist in interpolationCatalog. So the operator could pick ${filter} or ${moon.phase} from a menu and have it burned verbatim into the broadcast JPEG. Fixed by giving the picker a `variables` parameter and defining the watermark's real vocabulary as `watermarkVariableCatalog` next to the token map that answers it (live_stacking_broadcast_service.dart:39-105), passed at the call site (live_stacking_properties.dart:299-305). previewInterpolation gained a `catalog` parameter so the dialog's preview speaks the same language as the list.

2. THE CAPABILITY GAP THE FINDING NAMED. The NotificationNode's Title and Message are the sequencer's actual ${...} template fields — their hints advertise ${frame} / ${target.name} / ${time.local} — and they had no insert control at all. Added an opt-in `variables` slot to NodeTextInput (node_property_widgets.dart:136-150, 214-223) and wired both fields to interpolationCatalog (_capture_rich.dart:351, :367). The picker writes through the TextEditingController, which does NOT fire TextField.onChanged, so the insert is committed to the node explicitly — without that the variable appears in the field and is silently absent from the saved sequence.

3. THE LAST DEAD WIDGET. VariablePickerField (the wrapper form) still had zero call sites and no correct home — the app's other template fields use $TARGET syntax, not ${...} — so it is deleted (113 lines), along with the doc reference to it.
test: NEW packages/skotiq_core/test/services/live_stacking_watermark_vocabulary_test.dart — drives every watermarkVariableCatalog entry through the real LiveStackingBroadcastService.renderWatermark() and asserts none renders as its own literal, plus a control that ${filter} (sequencer catalog) DOES render literally. packages/skotiq_app/test/widgets/sequence/variable_picker_wiring_test.dart strengthened: it now asserts the button's `variables` is watermarkVariableCatalog and uses exact find.text on the placeholders (the previous find.textContaining('integration.hms') matched the field's own helper text behind the dialog and passed without a dialog at all). packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/sequencer/notification_properties_test.dart gains 2 tests: both template fields offer a picker over interpolationCatalog, and inserting a variable is committed to the node. variable_picker_test.dart's VariablePickerField group is retargeted at the button's dialog preview and gains a case that the preview honours the supplied vocabulary.
revert_check: (a) Deleted 'variables: watermarkVariableCatalog,' at live_stacking_properties.dart:301 -> variable_picker_wiring_test.dart RED ('Expected: same instance as [...]'). Restored; green. (b) Deleted both 'variables: interpolationCatalog,' lines at _capture_rich.dart:351,:367 -> notification_properties_test.dart RED on 'template fields offer a variable picker' and 'inserting a variable commits it to the node' (0 pickers found). Restored; 5/5 green.
caveats:
The vocabulary regression was live in the working tree; there is no evidence it ever shipped. The watermark catalog is a hand-maintained mirror of _watermarkTokens, which is why the new core test drives the real renderer rather than comparing two lists.

WHOLE-SUITE RESULTS (shared files were touched in both packages). skotiq_core: 5422 pass / 4 skip / 6 fail — all six in test/services/import/nina_sequence_fidelity_test.dart, proven pre-existing by re-running that file with my two core lib changes stashed (identical 6). skotiq_app: 2812 pass / 44 fail across 20 files — 40 of the 44 are 'Pixel test failed' whole-screen golden captures (captures_*_test.dart on 15 different screens, plus mosaic_project_screen_golden_test and public_screenshots_test), i.e. the known Linux-vs-Windows golden class; the remaining 4 are in framing (framing_hips_layer_wiring_test, framing_registration_test — another agent's live area) and mosaic timer-pending. I proved the one that could plausibly have been mine — screens/sequencer/captures_landscape_test.dart — is unrelated: with 'variables: interpolationCatalog' removed from both notification fields the diff is byte-identical (9.44% / 37838px and 7.17% / 28724px, exactly as with the change in). No failure line anywhere in the run references VariablePicker, NodeTextInput or watermarkVariableCatalog; all 11 mentions are passing progress lines from the new tests. dart analyze over both packages: 0 errors. dart format --set-exit-if-changed clean on all touched files.

Note on method: other agents were editing and running tests in this same working tree throughout, so full-suite numbers are only meaningful per-file. Every claim above is backed by a targeted re-run.
